expiresAt.description: When the access token expires, epoch milliseconds: what a refresh timer in the browser is scheduled from.

signedOut.description: `true` when a full account's grant had ended and the guest in this answer replaced it: the user was signed in and is not any more, so the UI offers a sign-in rather than silently showing a guest. `false` for every other answer, a guest whose own grant ended included — there was nothing to sign out of.

sessionId.description: The session id, in the `bearer` transport only, and only when this answer *created* the session: a guest minted because the request presented no id, or none the store still holds. An answer for a session the caller already presented carries none — the caller is holding that id already, and an answer delivered late (a refresh timer in another tab, arriving after a sign-in completed in this one) must not be able to put a retired id back in use. The cookie transport never puts the id in a body at all.

503.description: CAS cannot be used right now (`cas_unavailable`), or refused this client (`cas_rejected`) on the refresh or the guest grant. Or the session's lock was not granted in time (`session_busy`).

error.description: Why the handler refused; a caller branches on it. `cas_unavailable`: CAS, or whatever answered in its place, cannot be used right now. Transient; try again (503). `cas_rejected`: CAS refused this client's registration or the shape of its request. Not transient: an operator must act (503).

get.description: Stores the sign-in in flight, binds its `state` to this browser with a cookie, and sends the browser to CAS. A guest is force-refreshed first, so its fresh ID token can hint the upgrade. `302` is the cookie transport's answer, `200` the bearer transport's.
